{"v": 1, "title": "FIBO 2.0 Generate + Edit", "subtitle": "Change a picture you load, or make a new one, with FIBO 2.0 Edit Turbo in 4 steps. Switches write the prompt for you and make the result twice as big.", "author": "AusBoss", "layout": "card", "accent": "", "body": "[▶ AusBoss on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/@ausbossdev) · videos on these nodes and workflows

---

1. Load your picture.
2. Write the change: "Make it snow." With **Auto prompt** on, a few words are enough.
3. Press **Run**. A before and after slider shows your picture against the edit.
4. To make a new picture instead, switch **Edit a picture** off, write a prompt and set the size in **Latent Size**.

**FIBO 2.0 needs ComfyUI's latest development version (nightly)** until the next ComfyUI release: its support went into ComfyUI on 2026-10-21. A git install: `git pull` on master, then `pip install -r requirements.txt`. Without it, the run stops at **TextEncodeFibo2**, a node ComfyUI does not know yet.

**FIBO 2.0 is for non-commercial use only.** Its files are under CC BY-NC 4.0; for commercial use you need a licence from Bria.

### Switches

- **Edit a picture** on: the prompt changes the picture you load. Off: the prompt makes a new picture at the **Latent Size**.
- **Auto prompt** on: Qwen3-VL 8B writes the long prompt FIBO 2.0 reads, a description of the result in JSON, from your few words. For an edit it looks at your picture. What it wrote shows in **Show Text**. It takes about 6 to 9 seconds more and needs the Qwen3-VL 8B file below.
- **Upscale the result** on: SeedVR2 makes the result twice as big on each side and sharpens it. It needs the two SeedVR2 files below.
- The slider under **Save Image** shows your picture against the edit; a new picture shows on both sides. With **Upscale the result** on, a second slider shows the result before and after the upscale.

### Tips

- FIBO 2.0 Edit Turbo draws new pictures and edits in 4 steps at CFG 1. On an RTX 5090 a new picture takes about 2 seconds and an edit about 3 seconds. **Upscale the result** adds about 5 to 10 seconds.
- For an edit, say what changes and what stays: "Change her top to a red sweater. Keep everything else the same."
- To keep changing the same picture: pick **Erase** on the slider and paint where the edit should show (the rest stays your picture), press **Save**, drop the saved picture on the picture node, and run the next edit. **Copy**, a click on the picture node and Ctrl+V work too (Copy needs ComfyUI opened as localhost or https).
- Your picture is resized to 1 megapixel, the size FIBO 2.0 was made for, and the edit keeps its shape.
- Your own LoRAs for FIBO 2.0 go in the **LoRA Loader**.
- To change how Auto prompt writes, open the box **Write the prompt**: both instructions are plain text.
- FIBO 2.0 does not know famous people or game characters by name.
- If the run stops with "Value not in list", a file is missing. Download it from the list below.

### Uncensored text encoders (optional)

Versions of the two text encoders with the model's refusals taken out ("Heretic"), made by the community, not by Bria or Qwen. You don't need them; the workflow opens with the regular files picked.

- For FIBO 2.0's text encoder: [qwen3-vl-4b-heretic_int8_dynamic_convrot.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/ethanfel/Qwen3-VL-4B-Heretic-ComfyUI-ConvRot-INT8/resolve/main/qwen3-vl-4b-heretic_int8_dynamic_convrot.safetensors) → `models/text_encoders` · 4.84 GB. Pick it in **Text encoder**.
- For Auto prompt: [qwen3-vl-8b-heretic-1.3.0_fp8_e4m3fn.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/DreamFast/Qwen3-VL-8B-Heretic-1.3.0/resolve/main/comfyui/qwen3-vl-8b-heretic-1.3.0_fp8_e4m3fn.safetensors) → `models/text_encoders` · 10.02 GB. Pick it in **Text encoder for Auto prompt**.
- My quick test, one new picture and one edit with each on plain prompts: both load in this workflow and make normal pictures, and with the 4B the edit kept the picture as the regular file does.

FIBO 2.0 is by Bria AI; these are Comfy-Org's ComfyUI files.

nodes.title: Callout
Text - How a new picture's prompt is written
widgets_values:
You write prompts for FIBO 2.0, an image model that reads a JSON description of the picture to draw.

You receive a short idea from the user. Write one JSON object that describes the finished picture in rich detail.

How to write it:
- Keep everything the idea says. Fill in what it leaves open (the place, the light, the colours, the camera angle, the framing, small details) so it fits the idea and makes a strong picture.
- When the idea is about a person, frame them so their face and upper body read clearly (a medium shot or a close-up) unless the idea asks for a wide or full-body view.
- Every person in the picture is an adult. Write "a young woman in her twenties" where the user says girl, and "a young man in his twenties" where the user says boy or guy.
- A photograph unless the idea asks for another style; then set style_medium to that style and describe everything in it.
- Text: put in text_render only words the idea gives, copied letter by letter, and words that belong to an object by nature (STOP on a stop sign). Never invent titles or slogans. Otherwise text_render is [].
- Left and right are each person's own.

The JSON object has exactly these keys:
- "short_description": the picture in a few sentences, 200 words at most.
- "objects": up to five main things, people first. Each has "description", "location" (where in the frame), "relationship" (to the other things), "relative_size", "shape_and_color", "texture", "appearance_details" and "orientation". A person also has "pose", "expression", "clothing", "action", "gender" and "skin_tone_and_texture". A group of the same thing also has "number_of_objects".
- "background_setting": the place and everything in the background.
- "lighting": an object with "conditions", "direction" and "shadows".
- "aesthetics": an object with "composition", "color_scheme" and "mood_atmosphere".
- "photographic_characteristics": an object with "depth_of_field", "focus", "camera_angle" and "lens_focal_length".
- "style_medium": "photograph" unless the idea asks for another style.
- "artistic_style": three words at most.
- "context": what kind of picture this is, in one sentence.
- "text_render": a list of objects with "text", "location", "size", "color", "font" and "appearance_details", or [].

Write only the JSON object, with no words before or after it and no code fence. End with its closing brace.

The idea:
{user}

nodes.title: Callout
Text - How an edit's prompt is written
widgets_values:
You write prompts for FIBO 2.0, an image editing model that reads a JSON description of the finished picture.

You receive:
1. A picture.
2. A short edit request from the user.

Write one JSON object that describes the picture as it will look after the edit.

How to write it:
- Look at the picture closely first: each person (face, hair, expression, pose, what each hand does, clothes, jewelry), each object, the place, the light, the colours, the camera angle and the framing.
- Change only what the request asks for, plus what has to change with it (a new place brings its own light; rain makes the street wet). Everything else stays exactly as it is in the picture: the same people with the same faces and hair, the same pose, the same clothes, the same objects in the same places, the same framing, camera angle and lens, the same style.
